title: The Morning Brief: Scheffler breaks through with record-margin St. Jude win
dek: Scottie Scheffler ended his winless streak in emphatic fashion at TPC Southwind while European Championships history and a costly suspension in the AFL rounded out a busy weekend.
author: GoCheckMySports
key_fact: Scheffler's eight-shot St. Jude victory, the largest in the tournament's 68-year history, answered the season-long question of whether his string of close finishes would turn into a win.
bottom_line: Scottie Scheffler's eight-shot win at the FedEx St. Jude Championship, the largest margin in the tournament's 68-year history, turned a season of near-misses into a decisive result and secured him the FedEx Cup's No. 1 seed along with $23 million in bonus money. Cameroon claimed its first Wafcon title with a 3-0 win over Malawi, ending three prior final losses to Nigeria, while Amy Hunt's three golds at the European Championships set up a bid for a fourth in Sunday's mixed relay. In the AFL, Melbourne forward Jacob van Rooyen was suspended three matches for a strike that knocked out Port Adelaide's Aliir Aliir, and Washington's Marcus Mariota will miss the rest of the preseason with a sprained MCL. The reporting establishes clear results and disciplinary findings across each story, without extending into what any team or athlete does next. Sunday's mixed relay and next week's BMW Championship stand as the immediate checkpoints ahead.
body: The day's central fact is a number: eight. That is the margin by which Scottie Scheffler won the FedEx St. Jude Championship on Sunday, closing with a 4-under 66 to finish at 17-under 263. It is the largest winning margin in the tournament's 68-year history at TPC Southwind, surpassing John Cook's seven-shot win in 1996. Si Woo Kim finished second at 9-under, with Sam Burns and Alex Noren tied for third and Sungjae Im tied for fifth.

Saturday's story had framed this as a tighter race, with Scheffler holding a two-shot lead over Burns and Im entering the final round and chasing his first win since January after five runner-up finishes and five other top-4s this year. The final round settled that question decisively rather than dramatically. Scheffler's win also carries financial weight beyond the trophy: $3.6 million from the event's prize fund plus an additional $23 million in bonus money for holding the FedEx Cup's No. 1 position through next week's BMW Championship.

Elsewhere, the weekend produced two other clear results and one unresolved one. Cameroon won its first Wafcon title, beating Malawi 3-0 in Rabat behind two goals from Marie Ngah Manga and one from Naomi Eto, ending three previous final losses to Nigeria. At the European Athletics Championships, Amy Hunt won her third gold of the meet in the women's 4x100m relay and will attempt a fourth, historic title in Sunday's mixed 4x100m relay, which would make her the first athlete in the event's 92-year history to win four golds at one edition. Dina Asher-Smith, at 30, matched the championship record of seven career gold medals along the way. In the AFL, Melbourne forward Jacob van Rooyen received a three-match suspension for a swinging arm strike that knocked out Port Adelaide's Aliir Aliir, who failed his Head Injury Assessment. The ban costs Melbourne a forward for next week's game against the Western Bulldogs and potentially the club's first two finals matches.

On the injury front, Washington backup quarterback Marcus Mariota sprained his MCL on a noncontact play just four plays into Friday's preseason opener against Miami and will miss the rest of the preseason, leaving Jayden Daniels as the only immediately available starter at the position.

The why behind Sunday's golf result is mostly performance: the reporting describes a dominant closing round rather than any collapse from the field, with Kim's own 9-under finish still landing eight shots back. For Cameroon, the story frames the win as ending a specific pattern of final-round losses to one opponent, Nigeria, though the reporting does not explain what changed tactically. The van Rooyen suspension follows directly from a match review officer's finding of careless conduct, high contact and severe impact, a straightforward disciplinary process rather than a contested one, though whether Melbourne appeals is not yet known from the reporting.
Desk boards were not available this morning, so today's numbers rest entirely on the desk's own published stories.

The coming days offer several concrete checkpoints. Hunt's mixed 4x100m relay runs Sunday at approximately 20:35 BST, a single race that will decide whether she becomes the first athlete to win four golds at one European Championships. Scheffler moves to the BMW Championship next week as the FedEx Cup's No. 1 seed, where his form will be tested again after Sunday's breakthrough. Whether Melbourne appeals van Rooyen's suspension, and how the Demons manage their forward line without him against the Western Bulldogs and into the finals, remains to be seen. And in Washington, Daniels' health becomes the single point of concern at quarterback with Mariota out for the rest of the preseason.
